definition: The boundary macro-sequence, in its final form, is the following. integrate → project → [sweep → guards → handlers] iterated to quiescence (under the firing budget) → all due s_update calls → logging / I/O staging.
note: Used in 15 sections, first in §8.6 and defined in §10.6; g-boundary cites it unlinked. Draft: the boundary's final sequence: integrate, project, sweep-guards-handlers to quiescence, due s_update calls, then logging and I/O staging.

definition: This gives the epoch rule, which is the core of this section. An epoch here is the world one round's sweep produces. It is not the input epoch of §10.4. A handler executes against exactly the world its guard fired on
note: Coinage inventory bucket B maps it to input epoch, but §10.6 says it is not that epoch; used in §5.3 before its §10.6 definition. Draft: a handler runs against exactly the world its guard fired on, the sweep of the firing round.

definition: A trial evaluation computes a guard's value at one instant θ inside the step.
note: Used in §10.2 before its §10.4 definition and by g-sweep and g-localized without a gloss. Draft: a guard's value at one instant θ in a step, found by writing the interpolated state to the buffer and running the interior sweep.

definition: When such a transition should localize, write it in the gate form (gate) ? σ : -one(σ). The Bool factors go in the branch condition and the continuous factor in the value.
note: Called the gate idiom in §2.3:390, far from its §10.4 definition. Draft: a mixed predicate written (gate) ? σ : -one(σ), Bool factors in the condition and the continuous factor in the value, so it localizes.

definition: The guard's return type declares its detection policy. A guard returning Bool is boundary-detected. A guard returning the nominal scalar, the continuous sign form, is localized.
note: Umbrella term for two anchored entries; first used in §8.2 and defined in §10.4. Draft: how the framework finds a guard's crossing, fixed by the guard's return type, Bool boundary-detected or sign form localized.

term: event registers (prior, last-observed sample, firing count)
definition: Three registers per event decide the rule, all named normatively. The prior is the previous boundary's quiescent sample. The last-observed sample is initialized from the prior when the boundary opens and overwritten by every round's evaluation. The firing count for the boundary is incremented at each firing and reset when the boundary ends.
note: LOCAL to §10.6; g-prior defines one register and mentions the last-observed sample without defining it. Draft: per event, the prior, the last-observed sample and the boundary's firing count; only the prior crosses a boundary.

definition: A component's other eligible events are blocked, not lost. Each is re-decided in the next round, against the post-transition sweep.
note: Used in §5.3:1364 before its §10.6 definition; the blocked edge stays unconsumed in the registers. Draft: an eligible event held back because its component already fired one this round; it keeps its edge and is re-decided next round.

definition: This example follows one declaration to its compiled pairs and one hyperperiod (the span after which the tick pattern repeats).
note: Used from §9.2 before its §10.5 gloss; g-schedule names the hyperperiod chart only. Draft: lcm(Dᵢ) base ticks, the span after which the tick pattern repeats; the gate is modulo arithmetic so one hyperperiod is the complete truth.

definition: Admissibility is exact GCD arithmetic over the constraint pool: every anchor's period and every nonzero anchor offset τ
note: g-anchor mentions it in passing; used in §10.5 far from §9.2. Draft: every anchor's period and nonzero offset τ; an admissible Δt_base divides every entry, and the derived one is gcd(pool).

definition: The pair is kept in the canonical residue 0 ≤ Φ < D, so the component's ticks fall at base-tick indices Φ, Φ + D, Φ + 2D
note: First used in §9.1:4215 as c < m, defined in §10.5. Draft: the (D, Φ) pair kept with 0 ≤ Φ < D (and c < m for triples), preserved by relative composition.

definition: The grid diagnostics live on the Deployment and print from the pool, exactly
note: g-schedule names them as the Schedule's substrate. Leave-one-out refinement factors and prime attribution are its two forms. Draft: the Deployment's exact report of the coarsest admissible Δt_base, with per-entry blame, behind both the refusal message and the derivation info line.

definition: The nominal evaluation is a function of the Structure, and it returns three artifacts, Outputs, Events and the nominal Float64 activation
note: Step name used in §13.1 and §13.8 far from §9.1; g-outputs and g-events refer to it without an entry. Draft: the build step that probes every user function once at Float64 and returns Outputs, Events and the nominal activation.

definition: The structure step is pure declaration reading. No user stage code executes in it.
note: First glossed in §8.1:2392 (outside range); chapter 9 defines its work. Used in 8 sections. Draft: the build's first step, a tree walk reading declarations only and returning Structure; no user stage code runs.

definition: Real values are available because the stage-2 chain is probed in topological order.
note: Never defined as a name; g-activation says the probe chain is re-run. First use §8.4:3181. Draft: the stage-2 functions probed in topological order, each against the values upstream probes produced.

definition: The names are the pairing, and field order carries no semantics
note: Rule quoted in §14.7 and Appendix C; D-151. Draft: a NamedTuple return conforms by names and per-field types; field order carries no semantics at any author-framework seam.

definition: A discrete component or sub-assembly is scheduled by a sample_times entry in its enclosing assembly. The entry declares one (period, phase) pair in one of two unit systems
note: g-entry lists table, input, executor, roster, batch and condition entries but not this one (Relative or Absolute entry); 12 uses. Wiring entry and tap are outside my range.

definition: The wall-clock map is piecewise affine, re-anchored at every knee. A knee is a point where the map changes slope or offset. A pace change, an un-pause and a forgiveness re-anchor each make one.
note: About 12 pacer uses; g-pacing mentions re-anchor but does not define it, and the pacer sense collides with g-anchor (rate anchor). Lines 3569-3606 are an unrelated sense. Draft: the pacer's reset of its (t, τ) reference pair at a knee; debt is cleared and the counters record it.

definition: The wait mechanism is a hybrid sleep-then-spin with one knob. The pacer therefore sleeps toward deadline − margin and spins the remainder
note: Used in §12.2 far from §10.7; the margin knob is in g-control-plane. Draft: the pacer's wait, a task-yielding sleep to deadline − margin then a safepoint spin to the deadline.

definition: Budget exhaustion degrades; it does not throw. When a frame spends its budget, localization stops for the rest of that frame.
note: Doctrine cited by name as 'the no-throw doctrine of §14.8' and 'the doctrine of §10.4'; each budget entry states it separately. Draft: an exhausted budget sheds precision or firings with a named warning, never an error, and the run still replays identically.

definition: the check is an exact type match, with no convert-on-write
note: LOCAL to §9.5 (D-053). Draft: storing a stage return into a cell after converting its type; rejected at the nominal activation, where the check is an exact match.

definition: The store form is that every x_init, s_init and m_init value is a NamedTuple. A value that is not one is StoreNotNamedTuple.
note: LOCAL to §9.1; checked before the tier classifier reads the value. Draft: every x_init, s_init and m_init value is a NamedTuple.

definition: Probe values are strictly probe-scoped. Everything the probe writes is garbage once the build finishes.
note: LOCAL to §9.3; covers probe values, t = 0.0 and the placeholder Δt. Draft: a value fabricated for the probe that never doubles as an initial root input.

definition: The arrival sweep (the sweep that closes the integration step) at tₙ₊₁ raises the trigger
note: Coinage inventory bucket D; now 4 uses but all in §10.4. Demote to inline gloss if one section does not count as three places.

definition: The residual is deliberate stripping (ForwardDiff.value), a stated intent to discard partials, producing a silent zero in the Jacobian. The pinned leaf is the schema-visible freeze.
note: Uses in §9.5 and Appendix A:13227; LOCAL otherwise. Draft: discarding partials with ForwardDiff.value; declare the leaf Pinned{Float64} so the check holds the freeze to its word.

definition: Stage returns must have the same NamedTuple shape on every branch, the branch-shape rule
note: Coinage inventory bucket D; defined outside my range in §8.3 but now used 4 times, in §9.1 and §9.3 as well.

definition: Each kind of boundary has its own due set
note: g-due already states the due set.

definition: The execution form is a concretely-typed tuple of entries over statically typed cell storage
note: g-executor defines this compiled form.

term: epoch-caused edge / trajectory-caused edge / θ = 0 validation
definition: On trigger, the first act is a trial evaluation at the left end, the θ = 0 validation
note: g-input-epoch defines all three.

definition: Every discrete component's period is an integer multiple of a base tick period Δt_base
note: Alias; g-anchor also says anchor 0 is the base grid.

definition: The activation cache lives on the Build and holds only immutable compiled artifacts
note: g-activation ends on lazy activations; the cache could take a sentence there.

definition: Grid times are indexed, never accumulated
note: g-harmonic-grid states the rule in its last sentence.

definition: under the honest priors of §10.6
note: Inventory bucket B; confirmed.

definition: A stage returning bare (;) produces no ports at all, and is DeadStage
note: Two prose uses, one Appendix C identifier.

definition: Tracer activation names the global set-tracer
note: Two uses in one paragraph; the cycle classifier is defined in §13.8.

definition: the misplaced pin of §8.2
note: Inventory bucket D; still two uses.

definition: per component, its rate chain of Relative/Absolute links
note: Glossed inside g-structure and g-schedule.

definition: The face table is two-sided, and Structure answers it as a function over the declared wires
note: Glossed inside g-structure.

definition: Leave-one-out refinement factors are the first form. Prime attribution is the second form.
note: Two uses and one Appendix C citation.

definition: The Relative case is the affine law (§10.5) in anchor-tick units.
note: One use.

definition: A scope's base rate is its fastest relative member, and that member gets K = 1.
note: Two uses, one section.

definition: the step-boundary contract (at every boundary the §10.6 macro-sequence completes before a snapshot goes out)
note: Two uses; the 'central invariant' of the design.

definition: against the post-transition sweep
note: Inventory bucket D; still two uses.

definition: The four-body roster is fixed and total
note: One use.

definition: Exact match and embed-accept
note: One heading; the rule is a walking leaf accepting the scalar or Float64.
